title: Sepiapterin responsiveness registry study
summary:
In mid-2025, sepiapterin was approved by the EMA. It is approved for adults and children with PKU and hyperphenylalaninemia. In classic PKU patients, the effect was often less pronounced than in milder forms. Sepiapterin could be a promising new treatment, but its high cost and specific benefits for classic PKU still need to be clarified.

A responsiveness test should be performed to determine whether Sepiapterin will help an individual patient. Only patients who show a metabolic response are likely to benefit from the therapy.

Test results and additional data on medical history, genotype, BH4 response, and other relevant information are recorded in an online database.

The aim of this registry study is to evaluate the biochemical response to sepiapterin and provide information to support clinical decisions. To this end, the results of sepiapterin response tests from normal clinical practice are documented and analyzed to assess actual efficacy.

interventions.name: In this observational study children and adults with PKU who had a sepiapterin responsiveness test or with a sepiapterin responsiveness test planned in the future can be enrolled.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•Children and adults with a confirmed diagnosis of phenylketonuria (PKU).
•Sepiapterin treatment has already started or is planned following clinical routine measures
•A sepiapterin responsiveness test was already conducted or is planned in the future
•Written informed consent from patients, parents or legal guardians
Exclusion criteria:
•The individual, in the opinion of the investigator, is unwilling or unable to adhere to the requirements of the study
